title: This Fish Is the Kobayashi of the Sea - Nautilus
author: Devin Reese
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementZoologyThis Fish Is the Kobayashi of the SeaIt can swallow prey up to 10 times its weightDRBy Devin Reese4:00 PM CDT on October 15, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleWhile many of us were on vacation in July, marine biologists from SpeSeas were hard at work peering at eelpouts, squat lobsters, and carnivorous sponges. Hosted aboard the Schmidt Ocean Institute’s ship Falkor, the research group completed the most comprehensive deep-sea survey ever around the islands of Trinidad and Tobago, discovering 20 potential new species.Read more: “Behold, Crawzilla, the Not-Quite-Biggest Crayfish Ever Caught”Along the way, though, they got a whole new look at previously recorded species as well. Case in point: An ROV cruising about 1,259 meters below the sea surface secured footage of a black swallower fish that had just consumed prey many times its body size. The species (Chiasmodon niger) grows to only about 4 to 8 inches long, yet pursues fish as much as four times its length and 10 times its mass. It can eat such fish whole by dislocating its jaw and distending its stomach like a balloon, leaving it looking like a snake that’s eaten a rabbit. Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
